islandAreas.description: the island is home and exactly this many more areas, those nearest home's, round, its radius halfway out to the next (0: the radius below).

island.description: "home" plays home by roster, one area per kind she knows (the 10 kinds introduced at home and each kind whose island she's found, map.found: growing outward, its first areas the same; islandAreas its least, the kinds again past one each), its legends dealt each night, 1 in 5 areas; a kind's name (?island=fox) plays that kind's island, its own seed (where it lies on the sea chart) and size by phase (10 a phase), its roster that kind plentiful, 1-3 kinds new to its phase and the rest by bearing; empty, areas of random types as before.

found.description: the kinds whose islands she's found (the night's legends favour the others).

phase.description: an island grows out from home over its areas' neighbours, each step the area nearest home for the island's reach that way, by its phase's shape (shapes[phase], index 0 home: near-round; 1 gently lobed; 2 bays and a peninsula; 3 arms and inlets; 4 and 5 strongly irregular): lobes, how far its outline swells and shrinks round home (a share of its reach) over harmonics bumps; arms, how far its peninsulas reach past it (a share), armCount to of them, each armWidth radians across; bays, how deep its bays cut in, bayCount to of them; jitter, each area's own seeded nudge in areas (ragged edges).

coast.description: which areas are playable and which the buffer's goes by their centres' distance from home over the same seeded coast, up to amp of its radius in or out (0 for a perfect circle): harmonics gentle bays and headlands (from two round the island up), plus detail (a share) of finer wobble.

map.description: The forest: mapAreas x mapAreas areas cut by the fractal partition.

biomeLooks.description: How strongly an island's forests take its biome's look (art/flora/biomes.js), by its ring: strength for phase from's islands, strength the next ring out, and so on, the last for any further; each mixes the biome's look toward temperate's by 1 - strength (1 the full look).

shore.description: metres of bare shore round the water (no trees, nothing placed).

pad.description: how far from the water anything on foot stops.

koi.description: the share of lakes with koi in them (DECISION FOR ED).

biomeFrom.description: the island phase from which its lakes take the look of its compass biomes on the sea chart (frozen, lava, oasis, sinkhole, glacial tarn, tar pit, rust pool, lily pond; app/chartOutlines.worker.ts), before it plain water.

biomeFirstShare.description: the share of that first phase's lakes that take them, each lake seeded, the rest plain water; further out all of them, further in none.

lakes.description: Lakes: from phase 1 some of an island's areas are water, map.shapes[phase].lakes (fewest, most) of them, each lakeSize (fewest, most) areas, never home or its neighbours, the rest of the island still joined (rules/islandGrowth.ts placeLakes); no beaches but a small shore, their water lighter than the sea; she flies over them in the treetops but never lands on the water, and on foot she and every creature stop at the shore.

disc.description: its disc drawn in the sky past the rim at its bearing (hidden behind the world).

moon.description: each time the chart opens the moon rises over its edge at bearing from (degrees, 0 north, clockwise: -45 the north-west) over rise seconds, from just under the horizon to height degrees, then goes round once every turn seconds; every island's relief throws a shadow away from it, across the sea and into its own valleys, shadow its darkest (0 none, 1 black), the hills' shading following it.

edgeBand.description: (#746: "add empty sea around the edge of the map"): the empty sea past the furthest islands, the disc's radius beyond theirs as a share of it (0 as before; at most 0.6).

sailHold.description: Seconds the use button (E, Enter, the pad's square) or the mouse is held on an island at the map table's chart to sail there, its ring filling; let go early, nothing.

chart.description: The sea chart (the map table and chart.html; render/chart/seaChart.ts, render/chart/moon.ts).

islands.description: Islands other than home (the wave 2 finale's dream bubbles and the sea chart; rules/islandShape.ts, art/islands.js; Ed, docs/backlog/journey.md): coast, the coastline's knobs as map.coast's (amp, the most it strays from round, a share of the radius; harmonics, how many bays and headlands; detail, the finer wobble), stronger than home's so every island has a shape of its own, read at a bubble's 30 pixels.

grain.description: how far each of the sand's art pixels is lightened or darkened at random, 0.14 = ±7%; the sand and sea draw their art pixels doubled until each covers at least a screen pixel (render/ground.ts), so the grain stays chunky under the beach's far, low camera.

vary.description: the sand's width round the coast, width times e to the amp times a seeded smooth noise of harmonics bays and narrows; where the noise is lowest (below -rocky, of -1 to 1) it turns rocky, narrowing to rockyWidth metres; never under min.

decor.description: round the coast in sectors sectors, about finds finds a sector (shells, starfish, a conch, seaweed, pebbles; rocks on a rocky stretch), each sector with a trails chance of a trail of prints to prints footprints (bare feet, paws, hooves, a bird's, weighted by kinds) wandering along the sand and fading out; all of it on the wet and dry sand, the clear metres of it nearest the woods left bare.

dolphins.description: leaping off the east coast, within arc radians of due east, one every every to seconds, pair of them in twos, out to metres past the water's edge from her and ahead to metres north of that (away from the camera: the stargazing bend drops anything much more than 20 m ahead of her below the screen), each leap length metres along the coast and height high over time seconds.

kraken.description: off the west coast, within arc radians of due west, a slot every every seconds, chance of them holding a rising: tentacles to tentacles rising one after another out to metres past the water's edge from her and ahead to metres north of that, each over time seconds, and in head of them the dome of its head and its eye.

beach.description: The beach: sand over the last width metres inside her flight's edge (nothing grows or stands on it), the sea from shore metres past the edge, the hills eased over ease metres down to sand metres high where the sand starts and to sea metres at the water.

bushes.description: the share of the undergrowth and the ground cover left in its open middle.

arena.description: every area is mostly open within radius metres of its centre and its soundsystem, for fights (they range 15 to 45 m), and (Ed: softer edges; then, at v473, a smaller clearing and a long soft gradient from the area's edge to near its runestone) the woods thicken over a band band metres wide beyond it, across most of the area, along curve (linear: thinning in from right past the open middle; smooth: a slow start), lone trees and bushes thinning out into the clearing, its edge wobbled by noise (a share of the band) so it's no ring; both times fight.scale.

areaSizeVariance.description: (0-1) makes areas vary in size, some small, some large.

clearingSize.description: (0-1): how far out from an area's centre the ground stays fully open.

clearingFalloff.description: (0-1): over how much of the way to the border trees thicken to full density (small: crisp clearing edges).

gladeAmount.description: (0-1) of the woods is open in random glades about gladeScale metres across; trees sit on a staggered grid treeSpacingX by treeSpacingZ metres, so no two crowns pile up.

tufts.description: the share of the band the ground cover blends over (0: the tufts keep the exact border, as before; they lie on the area's own floor, which keeps its edge, and a cave mouth's bare ground taking a grassland's thick grass 40 m in read as wrong; 1 blends them as the trees); their cell (a legend circle's floor, an arena) stays the exact one either way.

areaEdgeBlend.description: Blended area edges: each tree and bush takes its look (its area type) from a point up to width metres away, the offset mostly the plant's own, drawn independently of its neighbours' (stray of it: 0.85, Ed's #887 feedback, so the kinds interleave tree by tree rather than in clumps; it was 0.5), the rest a smooth noise scale metres across so the band doesn't run dead straight; the neighbour's share ramps from about half at the border to none width metres in.

groundBlend.description: How neighbouring areas' floor textures meet (Ed, v160): the border is warped by noise in two octaves (up to warp metres over about 40 m, and fine metres over about 6 m), so it meanders rather than following the texture's grid; across a band metres wide the two floors mix pixel by pixel, by noise and (dither) an ordered dither, like grass creeping into dirt.

layout.description: every area's runestone stands on a rise and every legend clearing lies in a hollow, rise and dip times the hills' amplitude high and deep (0.15 of 40 m: 6 m), each easing out over reach metres (kept short and low: the stones are about 110 m apart, a clearing about 65 m from its stone, and the slopes must stay under the camera's sightline) (the plateaus then level each one, so a stone tops a knoll and a clearing sits in a dell); trees grow up to trees (a share) thicker in the lowest ground and thinner on the highest, by the land's height over half the hills' amplitude (most of it lies within that).

ground.description: The ground's fake relief (Ed, v171: so the ground doesn't look flat): low rises and hollows from noise about relief.scale metres across, tilting the ground's lighting by relief.strength (0 flat) so the witch's light and the campfires pick out the bumps, and hollows shaded darker by relief.shade.

wisps.description: Will-o'-the-wisps in the wild areas: a seeded chance per square of ground (cell m) within reach of her; none within partyNear of a partified area, the full chance from partyFar; height [low, high] m, drift m, a cycle of period s (fade in, linger, fade out, gone); core and halo size in art pixels; colour.

hue.description: the twilight's colour (a cool violet dusk, against the party's amber).

light.description: its pool, filling the circle and soft at its edge.

edge.description: the ring at its edge at full (a quarter of it always marks the circle), which brightens with the witch inside it or a quest sigil or relic put down in it, easing at edgeEase a second.

motes.description: per to a clearing, rising rise metres a second to height metres, size art pixels, in hue and sat at bright.

glades.description: The sleeping legends' clearings: art builder 1 places them (the map's glades); until then one round each sleeping legend, radius metres across with the legend top of the way toward its top.

carrier.description: "island" that island's kind's legend, braced under the Ent, its back about 13 m up and the Ent's trunk that much shorter, so the deck stays where it is (home, the Ent's own island, has none, nor has a map that isn't an island); a kind's id (e.g. "bear", or ?carrier=bear) that kind's everywhere; "none" no one.

treehouse.description: The witch's treehouse, home: its foot (the Terrace's middle; clear metres round it) stands gap metres beyond the dancefloor's ring of speakers (so however many speakers or how far out, it stays outside them; 22 keeps the oak's rooms, up in its crown, clear of the dancefloor's clearing), at angle degrees (-135: north-west; -90 due north, straight up the screen), always facing south, to the floor and the camera; and keeps a clearing of clear metres round its foot (at least the art's footprint: 8.2 m for the v2 tower); its lantern and fairy lights light lightReach metres round at lightStrength.

home.description: Home's area: the map is cut with home first, a circle round the dancefloor out past the treehouse's footprint (its distance and clear) and margin metres more all home's; the areas round it are cut round it, their centres kept at least gap of an area beyond the circle.

featured.description: one of ids (seeded) placed on a map at its chance, in an area it suits if there is room, else in any.

scenes.description: Scenes: small vignettes (a farmyard corner, a bus stop, a picnic gone wild...) and large landmarks (a cemetery, a car park, ruined churches and temples, castle ruins...), each a few pieces counting as one, each at most once per map.

grounds.description: Old playgrounds and sports grounds (the relics art's arrangements): an area has one with chance (not home), off to the side of its centre, keeping a clearing of radius metres (per kind) where nothing grows.

minFromStone.description: its edge at least this many metres from its area's runestone (where the soundsystem comes), clear of the stone's clearing and the party's dance space; a small area with no such spot takes the farthest that fits (logged).

minFromOtherStones.description: its edge at least this many metres from every neighbouring area's runestone too, always (not relaxed for a small area).

glint.description: how much the grooves catch the light while its legend sleeps (0, off: Ed's call later).

floor.description: on, old flagstones about slab metres across, the legend's sigil carved into them as dark grooves, overgrowth (0.5 as drawn, up to 1 for more) moss, grass and litter over them so the carving shows only in pieces.

rim.description: art builder 3's rim kit (#262) round its edge, a piece every spacing metres of it at chance, out metres past its radius and up to spread more (on its ring, never its floor), none on a path nor within gap degrees of due south.

grove.description: round the circle's ragged edge the forest swells, strongest at the edge and easing out (smoothstep) over reach metres to the area's own: there trees stand at up to density (a chance a tree spot), up to tallest of them the area's two tallest kinds, drawn up to scale times bigger, each tree's strength jittered by jitter either way so no ring or step shows; open in front gap degrees either side of due south (toward the camera), easing in over soft degrees more.

fit.description: each circle sized to its legend as drawn asleep (config/legend-footprints.json, measured by node tools/legends/footprint.mjs), its sleeping body fitting where it lies with margin metres to spare, never smaller than species (or radius) gives it, never more than max metres (past about 25 a circle can't be placed in its area clear of the runestones); in a legend area of its own (legends.areas) at most areaMax metres, at the area's heart, clear of the runestones round it by minFromOtherStones.

legendClearing.description: Each area's sleeping legend lies in a small circular clearing of its own, where no tree or decor stands: radius metres across from its middle (species: a radius for that legend, sized to fit it: half its sleeping width plus 4 m), a soft ring edge metres wide marking it on the ground, and the legend lying top x radius north of the middle (the circle's far side from the camera), the open floor in front.

relics.description: Modern relics (cars, trolleys, cones, highway slabs, a phone box, a sofa...): one chance per spacing-metre cell (chance, steered by the area's decor share of modern), nearRoad times as likely within 20 m of a road or railway; never on a path, in a central clearing or a ground; at least minGap metres from the next relic (Ed, v147: too numerous).

walls.description: Wall objects as features (Ed, v147), per area: man-made and linear ones (garden walls, hedges, brambles, rock walls) as runs [min,max] of runLength [min,max] pieces joined end to end, along a path where one passes (with a gateway gap gateChance of the time; a garden's flower beds in a row along them); henge stones as rings [min,max] of ringStones [min,max] (the first round the shrine, others ringRadius [min,max] metres across in a glade), an avenue leading in avenueChance of the time, and a lone stone loneChance; water, reeds and boulders as clumps [min,max] of clumpSize [min,max] within clumpRadius metres.

mix.description: each family's share times its factor, 1 as each area authors it.

footprint.description: metres round a decoration kept clear of soundsystems, the dancefloor, the treehouse and set pieces (plus reserveMargin).

decor.description: Decorations scattered as discoveries: one chance per spacing-metre cell, of a ruin (ruins), a rock (rocks) or a freak tree (freak), each at least minGap metres from the next (Ed, v147: too numerous); fewer under dense canopy; never in an area's central clearing (openness under clearing), on or within pathGap metres of a path, or by the dancefloor.

linkChance.description: the share of neighbouring areas joined by a meandering path.

deadEndChance.description: the share of areas with a path out to nothing.

pathHalf.description: half each corridor's width (metres), kept clear of trees, with bushes thick along the edges for edgeBushes metres (bushBoost times as many); streams [min,max] long streams winding across the map (and short ones join wet areas that touch), streamHalf metres half-wide; along a railway, every landmarkSpacing metres, a landmarkChance of a landmark (a wagon, a carriage, a platform, a gantry) and otherwise sometimes a signal post; verge posts along roads every vergeSpacing metres; every 3D piece at least pieceGap metres from the next.

railBroken.description: the share of the railway that's broken, where trees grow between the sleepers (treesOnBroken times the usual chance).

pieces.description: false places none of these 3D pieces at all.

fingerposts.description: a fingerpost by each footpath where it comes into a clearing (the prop generator's; the game turns it on: app/linkParams.ts); the two flights of stairs are finds, each at most once per map, by the clearing of a ravine, rocky slope, cave mouth or stone shrine.

paths.description: Paths, roads and railways (Ed): far fewer since 2026-10-11.

setPieceChance.description: the share of areas, among the types that have a set piece, that show theirs.

setPieceFootprint.description: Gameplay is placed first, then scenery keeps clear of it: a set piece's footprint (setPieceFootprint metres round its middle, times setPieceScale) stays reserveMargin metres clear of every soundsystem's spot (soundsystemFootprint metres round it, reserved from the start) and of the dancefloor's clearing; a set piece with no room left is left out.

treeDensity.description: treeHeight and crownWidth scale the art's trees (1 is the Art Lab's size; crowns widen with treeHeight too, crownWidth is the total).

autumn.description: each tree's lit leaf colour drifts toward its own autumn colour (gold, orange, red, crimson or purple, by its first seed) by up to autumn of the way (its own share of it, some trees barely at all), kept at the brightness the night's moonlight gave it, so a red tree is as dark as its neighbours.

value.description: its leaves' brightness scaled by 1 + value times the second seed (on the pixels its sway mask marks as leaves: the wood is untouched; both halves alike).

hue.description: its lit leaf colour's hue turned either way by up to hue degrees times the first seed.

leafJitter.description: Each tree's own leaf colour: every tree is dealt two fixed seeds from where it stands (-1 to 1 each).

treetop.description: the share of it seen over the treetops (gentler).

wind.description: Wind sway on leafy things (Ed, v171): trees (both halves together, from the foot) and undergrowth lean with gusts that travel across the forest: strength metres at the top of a crown, gusts moving at speed m/s, gustScale metres across; Walls and set pieces stand still.

groundCover.description: Tufts of grass, fern, heather, reeds, moss and clover on the ground round the witch (Ed, v171: so the ground doesn't look flat), in ground mode only: density (times each area type's groundCover.density in area-types.json; ?grass=0..2 scales it live), out to the canopy hole round her, at most radius metres (fading out towards it), at most cap at once; one chance every spacing metres, worked out cell metres square at a time, within budgetMs of each frame; they sway in the wind by sway of their height and part round her and nearby creatures by part.

density.description: Tree density is a field, not two states: each area's own density (its layout in art/areas.js) times a patch noise patchScale metres across, from patchMin to patchMax times (dense patches, sparse patches, glades), times the area's pattern (groves, stands, rings, rows, thicket, edges only), times the clearings (soft edges); and lone trees at lone density almost everywhere, so open ground isn't empty.

treeCap.description: The tallest tree variants (tall, giant) can be drawn squeezed: any height over from metres keeps only keep of the rest.

pins.description: The HUD's pointers as map pins over their subject (render/indicator.ts): gap is how far (screen pixels) the arrow's tip floats over the subject's drawn top.

canopyReach.description: in the treetops, tree crowns alone (no trunk, shadow or undergrowth) are drawn out to this many metres (at most haze.far) where the budget has pulled the rest in closer, so the canopy stays whole to the horizon on a slow machine; 0 off.

acceleration.description: how quickly she reaches her speed or stops in the treetops (per second; higher is snappier).

cameraPull.description: how far the camera draws back at full boost (a share of its distance).

treetop.description: Treetop flight (Ed: a high top speed and momentum; the ground stays snappy): pressing a direction reaches treetopSpeed in about 0.3 s (acceleration); holding it within boostAngle degrees builds boost over boostTime seconds, up to boost times treetopSpeed; her heading turns toward the input at turnRateSlow degrees a second below sharpTurnSpeed of cruise, falling to turnRate at cruise (half that at full boost), so the size of her swoop grows with her speed (Ed); a turn of 90 degrees or more bleeds boost sharpTurnBleed times a second, and above brakeAt of cruise she skids in the brake pose; letting go, she glides to a stop over about glideTime seconds.

leanAt.description: the share of the top speed above which she leans into her flight.

facing.description: she (and every creature) faces the viewer unless clearly heading up the screen, within awayEnter degrees of straight up (and stays turned away until past awayLeave); sideways, down or stopped faces the viewer.

riseCooldown.description: After she lands she can't rise again for this many seconds.

cooldown.description: One cooldown for her dodge and her take-off: shared on, a counter in seconds draining a second a second; a dodge adds dash.cooldown, a take-off rise, a landing riseCooldown (the Jet nozzles halve both of the last: config/broom-parts.json).

knock.description: The witch knocked back and staggered by a blow: thrown straight away from the blow, base metres for any blow (bites, swipes, shots) plus scale times the attack's own knockback (combat.json; so a maul, quake or slam sits in between), at least charge metres when it rams her (a charge, or a leap landing on her), at most max; eased off at ease a second (like a creature's knockback), straight through scenery, nudged to the nearest clear spot at the end if she'd rest inside a trunk, rock, speaker, soundsystem or the treehouse (the blink's clearances).

witch.description: Speeds per mode, and how long rising and descending take.

stack.description: The sigil stack above the witch's hat: scale (of the sigils' size), offset (the gap between her hat tip and the bottom sigil, in sigil heights), gap (between sigils, in sigil heights).

grace.description: seconds after a hit in which no other blow lands, so a pack striking together takes one hit, not all three.

slashScale.description: her claw slashes' size relative to her.

slashGlow.description: their glow, the berries' light drawn in the scene along each stroke so the bloom takes it.

witchHealth.description: The witch: she takes hits (one point each, whatever hits her) before she's knocked out; one comes back every repairTime seconds, the timer starting over whenever she's hit, so to heal she has to get right out of the fight.

legendsLoyal.description: leashed legends stay with her (false: they're let go too: 'they're too old for this'; only a party legend is ever leashed now, and it's always let go).

dropHat.description: she drops her hat where she went down and wears none till she stands on it and presses the sigil button (E), which puts it straight back on (never into the stack; on top of a sigil, the hat comes first); a 🎩 pointer shows the way meanwhile.

dim.description: how much the screen dims round her while her hat floats off, from the knockdown to her sparkle away (her spot and the hat left lit); no hat, no dim.

rise.description: the house (rules/treehouse.ts): back at the magic circle after a knockout, she rises out of its floor over rise seconds, then walks to her decks and scratches for the rest of the wait.

candleStep.description: one candle for every candleStep seconds of the wait (1 or 0.5), white for the base wait, red for the extra from knockdowns in a row; the red burn first.

knockout.description: Knocked out: she collapses where she is; her sigil stack lets go from the bottom up, one every releaseEach seconds (releaseMax caps the whole release, 0 no cap; an empty stack waits emptyBeat seconds), each animal turning happy where it stands; then she sparkles out and back in behind her decks in the treehouse over teleport seconds.

buffer.description: a press up to this many seconds before she can blink (still recharging, landing, staggered) waits and blinks the moment she can.

toCursor.description: on, she blinks toward the ground under the cursor (or the way the right stick points), the way she faces when the cursor is within aimDead metres of her, and with nothing to aim by (touch) the way she's steering; off, always the way she's steering.

dash.description: The dash, a blink: on the ground only, she vanishes and reappears distance metres the way she's moving in one step, then cooldown seconds before the next.

hats.description: the spell hats she owns, a comma list or * for every one.

parts.description: her broom's parts, a comma list of ids from config/broom-parts.json (the page sets it from her save, localStorage witch.broom, fitted at the Workshop's bay; ?parts= for one load); the bare broom, none, has no spell and no quick take-off, and a complete set gives its spell.

speed.description: the Speed broom, her speed times mult for duration seconds, then cooldown seconds to recharge.

healing.description: the Healing ring, within radius m of it she heals a hit every `every` seconds while hurt.

battering.description: the Battering broom's blink stuns every wild and enraged creature within width m of its line for stun s.

leyjump.description: the Ley jump broom, cast, puts her at the ley line's pulse; cooldown s.

pound.description: the Ground pound broom, cast, rises or lands at once, knocking wild and enraged creatures within radius m back push m, and landing stuns them stun s; cooldown s.

stealth.description: the Stealth broom: creatures don't see her unless she threw a 💌 or put down or picked up something in the last reveal s; ones that went for her keep on while she's within range m, then lose her.

harvest.description: the Harvest hat, put down, grows berries berries in a ring radius m round it, at most once every every s (the same ring, moved: uneaten ones move with it).

dowsing.description: the Dowsing hat, put down, points to the nearest relic for time s.

sentry.description: the Sentry hat, lying there, throws a 💌 at the nearest invitable creature within range m every every s (Ed: larger ranges).

slingshot.description: the Slingshot hat catches her 💌s flying within catch m, circling it radius m out, holds them hold s and flings each at the nearest invitable creature within fire m, at most max at once.

gathering.description: the Gathering hat, picked up again, brings every sigil of hers within range m back to her stack (Ed: all sigils in range).

bramble.description: the Bramble hat slows wild and enraged creatures within range m of it (Ed: 30 m).

mine.description: the Mine hat, put down, stuns wild and enraged creatures within range m for stun s, at most once every every s.

lullaby.description: the Lullaby hat, put down, sends wild creatures (not enraged) within range m to sleep for time s, at most once every every s; one wakes when a 💌 lands on it.

cyclone.description: the Cyclone hat, on putting it down and every every s while it lies there, catches wild and enraged creatures within radius m, sweeps them round it at spin turns a second for time s, lifting them up to lift m, then flings them fling m outward over flingTime s, stunned stun s after they land; never hers, happy ones or legends, and never hurt.

nursing.description: the Nursing hat heals her own creatures within range m of it, rate of their health a second (0.1: whole again in ten seconds).

spells.description: Spells: two slots, a hat and a broom, each with a spell or none (the plain ones), the hat's chosen in the creator (or ?hat=), the broom's the set its parts complete.

width.description: metres across on the ground and over the treetops.

fade.description: how it fades along its length (eased out: bright for its first stretch, then thinning to nothing; higher keeps it bright longer), its width tapering with it.

sparks.description: the broom's little amber sparks as well.

trail.description: Her flight trail: a ribbon of glow along her path, fading to nothing at its tail, in the colour of the area she's over (eased over colourEase seconds as she crosses into the next).

swoopTrail.description: The party witches' swoop trails: while one swoops she leaves a ribbon in her trail's look, bright and in rainbow colours, each witch starting at her own hue, the colours running along it (hueSpread turns of the wheel a metre) and shifting over time (hueSpeed turns a second), so a crowd of swoops reads as fireworks over the canopy.

berries.description: Berries and evolving (Ed): every area has bushesPerArea berry bushes (normal bushes of that area) and perArea [min, max] berries on distinct ones at the start.

arc.description: the height (m) its lob rises over the straight line from her hand to the ground at its range, where it lands, with a puff (drawn only: the rules fly it flat).

hits.description: letters to fill it, by level (baby, young, adult); it drains drain of a full meter a second when not being hit, from config/states.json's affection.drainDelay seconds after the last.

fireSlow.description: her ground speed while firing, times this (Ram's Steady buff takes it away).

linger.description: a 💌 that met no one rests where it came down this many seconds, fading over the last lingerFade, at most lingerMax at once (drawn only: it's no hit).

spin.description: a 💌 in flight lies flat and turns about the upright this many times a second (drawn only); when it lands it stops and lies flat.

orbit.description: the 💌 ring circles a creature at scale times its body radius (movement.json bodies) plus gap metres, at least min, and wider still when it holds many.

invites.description: The 💌 invite, replacing the proximity chat when on: on the ground she shoots spinning 💌s, aimed with the cursor (click fires) or the right stick (a trigger fires), or 1 toward the cursor.

invite.description: The old proximity chat: on the ground, she talks by herself (no button: Ed, v244) to the nearest invitable creature within talkRange metres, and sticks with it; you chat in emoji for talkTime seconds (babies, young, adults), taking turns every turn seconds (babies, young, adults), then it is invited and leashed to you.

win.description: The end of the route: the last wave landed, a pointer to the enraged animal nearest the centre while any lives (enraged legends don't count; retarget: seconds between re-picks); none left, the victory lap: the pulse races back along the route to home at lapSpeed m/s, every stone it passes firing its fireworks; home reached, the night won: the dealt legends wake (bar any still enraged, which go back to sleep, their islands not found) and dance in place on its far side, north of the dancefloor beyond the conga, behind everything from the north-facing camera: on arcs legendGap m outside the conga's circle, legendRow m apart, legendSpace m between them, from due north out to legendArc degrees across, clear of the treehouse, the island's sigil flares on the dancefloor (drawn on over flareDraw s, held flare s), every other animal joins one conga line round it (congaSpeed m/s, congaGap m apart, a circle of at least congaRadius m, as big as the line needs), walking to its place at joinSpeed m/s (out of her sight, seen m off, simply there); settleAfter seconds after, it settles: the guidance pins lead her home.

length.description: how far a leashed creature roams from its leash point (you, or its sigil on the ground).

runSpeed.description: how fast it hurries back when out of range (m/s).

pickRadius.description: how near a placed sigil you must be to pick it up.

spacing.description: how close two sigils may be put down (keep it above pickRadius, or a blocked spot picks up instead of fizzling).

runeRadius.description: how near (m) she picks up a happy creature's rune, a relic's sigil or her hat.

hatHold.description: seconds she holds the sigil button on the ground, with nothing it picks up or puts down, to put her hat down at her feet (just a marker; a press over it puts it back on; rules/hat.ts putHat).

placedThrough.description: how bright a placed sigil shows where grass, bushes, trees or other scenery hide it (0 hidden, 1 as bright as in the open); never through the witch.

sigilGlyph.description: every sigil glyph from the leash atlas (placed, happy runes, the ghost, a relic's, her stack, the treetop projection, one walking home after a knockout) is drawn at sigilGlyph times its colour (0.5: under the bloom's threshold, so it doesn't bloom into a disc on lit ground; 1 as bright as before), and the soft halos under placed sigils, ready runes and relic sigils and round a relic in her stack at sigilHalo times their old strength (0: none).

sigilBacking.description: under every sigil lying on the ground (placed, a happy creature's rune, the ghost, a relic's) a near-black disc in chunky 2-px cells with a lighter outer step, as wide as the glyph's own pixels times size, at dark (0: none), then the glyph painted opaque in its full neon at ink times how much it shows, under the dim added glyph (sigilGlyph).

runeGap.description: a happy creature's rune lies south of it (down the screen), and a parked animal roams round a point the same way north of its sigil, by its size: its body radius, half the sigil with its backing, and runeGap metres between (rules/runeOffset.ts; it was a fixed restAbove, 5 m).

hex.description: on the ground the sigil button works on a world-fixed hex grid, size metres between neighbouring cells (6 with the rank sigils, their ranks.hex; 4 before them, leash.spacing's density, as ?sigils=old still has it; 0: put down freely where she stands, as before).

runs.description: with the sigil button held on since a press that picked a sigil up, she keeps picking up any sigil she runs over (her placed ones, happy creatures' runes, a relic's); held since a press that put one down, moving into each empty hex puts down the next (a press that did nothing starts no run, so holding E with nothing to do still puts her hat down).

runePull.description: on the ground, the nearest happy creature with its rune within radius (m) trots toward her at speed (m/s), stopping stop (m) from her, so its rune comes to her.

grounded.description: weight is the most the creatures following her may weigh, together, before she can't take off (their sigils in her stack, each at its leash.weight.levels weight times its species' strength, however near; parked ones at a sigil on the ground don't count, nor babies; 2 is one adult of normal strength, three young 2.4, two 1.6; 0 turns it off).

drag.description: moving away from the pull, that part of her speed is divided by 1 + drag x load (her input still steers).

drift.description: she drifts toward the pull at up to that share of her top speed, reached at an extreme load.

rise.description: rising takes 1 + rise x load times as long.

sink.description: over the treetops, loaded, she sinks by sink x load of the climb a second (at most sinkMax), to floor (of the climb, just over the crowns) while she flies on, and all the way down to land if she stops or her load reaches extreme; unloaded, she floats back up.

babyGround.description: a baby's weight on the ground (the treetops' is weight.levels), so 8 fill either allowance; a baby's species strength doesn't count, and in the line its leash's tension is measured from its place in the line.

weight.description: sigil weight: each sigil in her stack (placed ones weigh nothing) pulls her toward its creature by how taut its leash is (0 within 0.85 of length, up to maxTension a leash length further, however far: a far traveller can't pin her) times its weight (levels: baby, young, adult, legend; times its species' combat.json strength).

babies.description: her leashed babies following her on the ground walk in single file along where she's been, in stack order (the stack's bottom one first), gap metres apart; while she's in a fight they scatter, scatter metres or a quarter more off to the side away from the first attacker, for the whole fight: from the moment something goes for her or one of hers (closing in or winding up, not on the hit), the same way throughout, back into line once nothing has for calm seconds; one more than farAt metres from her (about off the screen) moves at farSpeed m/s, so it's with her in seconds.

ranks.description: on, every leash sigil (her stack, placed sigils, happy runes, the ghost, the treetop projection, the bond) is its bare glyph, no ring or disc, glyph metres across on the ground, in its rank's colour (colours: baby, youth, adult, legend; the species' neon stays the world's: borders, stones, fireworks, dancefloor, holograms, chart), with embers rising off its strokes (embers.count at once, each size metres, rising rise metres, by rank; in her stack stack of that), under a dark shade in the glyph's own shape (not a disc); a youth in her stack shows two rows of round dots off to its right, one a berry it eats on the move (toEvolve less the last, eaten at a placed sigil), at most dotsPerRow a row, bright eaten and dim not, pulsing when ready; and the hex grid is hex metres (leash.hex.size).

bond.description: how a creature shows its tie to its sigil (rim: a glow at its feet in the sigil's colour; sparks: one spark every sparkEvery seconds from sigil to creature, staggered; thread: a dotted line only under strain).

scale.description: every length in a fight times this (attack ranges, lunges, area radii, beam widths, knockback, the packs' patterns and spacing, pursuit and guard reach, aggro).

speed.description: every fight speed times this (running, charging, lunging, shots).

momentum.description: how heavily creatures in a fight change speed and turn: their accelerations, braking and turn rates divided by it (2: twice as heavy).

contact.description: it hurts every foe it touches on the way, once each (her grace making one charge one hit).

miss.description: a charge that struck nothing stands winded that many seconds after (stars round its head), an opening for her 💌s.

charge.description: every species' charge (movement.json) scaled: reach its run's time and overshoot past its target, turn its turn rate (lower: wider arcs), brake how hard it slows (lower: more momentum).

fight.description: The fight's scale and speed: fights are drawn and played at the ground camera's scale, creatures running at about the witch's speed and their patterns about 50 m across.

turn.description: its heading swings at most turn / (1 + its speed / k) degrees a second (also divided by fight.momentum), slowing to turn tighter when she's far off its heading, so a fast one sidestepped overshoots in an arc.

delay.description: it steers for where she was that many seconds ago (a short trail of her places), so a sidestep or blink fools it a moment.

chaseLead.description: seconds of her velocity it leads her by when just chasing (0: none).

strikeLead.description: times the lead its telegraphed attacks take (a melee wind-up's tracking, dodge.a.lead; a charge's lane, dodge.b.chargeLead; a leap, fight.leap.lead; a swoop's dive; shots and lobs, dodge.b.lead).

classes.description: each class's values (heavy: dodge.a.heavy's species; light: those with the nimble or swarm trait; normal: everyone else), and a species may set its own in its folder (art/creatures/<id>/creature.js movement.momentum).

creatureMomentum.description: Creature momentum, chasing the witch only (fights between creatures, legends and marchers as before): on its run-in and its wind-up (a pack's tell and combo too), never its committed lunge, which goes where the wind-up aimed, reaching up to a quarter again its usual length if the run-in left it short, so a strike that starts stays reliable.

legendFlash.description: how much bigger and longer a legend's blow flashes than anyone's (its flash 1 + 2 × legendFlash times; 0.5, twice: Ed's decisions panel, config/decisions.json).

attackFx.description: How attacks feel on screen, a party not a fight: windupSquash, how low and wide an attacker crouches as its wind-up nears the blow (at most windupMax seconds of it shown); lungeStretch, how far it stretches out in its lunge; squash, how flat a hit squashes the one it hits, springing back past its shape over squashSecs seconds; a knock-back thrown faster than tumbleKnock m/s tumbles: up tumbleHeight metres (at most 1.5 times that for the hardest) for tumbleSecs, over on its back from turnFrom to turnTo of the way (one slow beat, never a strobe), landing with a squash.

packs.description: pack combat, on by default and on the pause page to turn off for testing: on, packs of config/packs.json's kinds (home's ten and Phase 1's eleven) fight in combos (the nearest lunges, the ones at range fire where a dodge would go, the one behind her throws the special), fall back by their kind's retreat between combos, and her own pack combos without retreating.

aggro.description: wild creatures go for party animals within this, and for the witch anywhere in their area.

leaveArea.description: a wild one chasing the witch gives up once she's this far past its area's edge, and turns back home (besiegers keep witchLose: they give up once she's out of their area, out of range and this far off).

pursuit.description: how far from her (or its sigil, guarding) a party animal chases a foe before giving up.

pursuitRun.description: how fast it closes in while over 30 m off (so an area's creatures are onto her in a few seconds when she lands in it).

fightRun.description: how fast a creature runs in a fight (m/s), when its movement profile doesn't say (movement.json speed).

reaction.description: seconds before a creature that has just noticed something goes for it.

shake.description: how hard a legend's quake shakes the screen (0 none).

daze.description: seconds a wild creature knocked down in a fight lies stunned (nothing attacks it, it attacks nothing, she can still invite it; it counts as present for its legend, and no siege takes it) before it runs off home.

defendRadius.description: her animals following her within this many metres of her go first for anything attacking her, spread over her attackers; farther off, following her, one fights back only at what's on it itself (and parked, guarding or travelling ones carry on as they were): never pulled across to her fight.

taunt.description: a creature after her that one of her animals in her fight hits turns on that animal instead, with chance chance, for time seconds (a lunge at her already under way lands first; then it may come back to her).

combat.description: Combat (Stage 4; the attacks themselves are data in config/combat.json; lengths and speeds at the fight's scale: see fight).

notice.description: Creatures notice the witch on the ground within radius metres (Ed's playtest: a larger responsive area makes them feel alive): resting ones turn to look at her; babies of a curious kind come up to about curious metres from her, skittish ones keep about skittish metres off (config/combat.json temperament).

heavy.description: chasing her, those species run at up to speed m/s (above her walk) built up at accel m/s each second, their charges swinging toward her at home degrees a second as they run, so a burst or a blink gets clear and a long retreat is run down (the snail, hedgehog and woodlouse left slow, the last two with their rolling charges; the mole with its own burrow); her blink keeps her untouchable for gone seconds (dash.gone otherwise); and at most tokens creatures wind up or strike at her at once (swarmTokens when swarm or more are on her), the rest keep their places.

dodge.description: Dodging matters: against the witch only (fights between creatures as before).

on.description: false lets them roam the whole area as before.

stoneIdle.description: Hostile creatures gather near the runestone: a wild area's own hostile young and adults (not its babies, its legend or its circle's baby, nor a friendly area's, nor happy, leashed or enraged ones) start, roam and nap anywhere in a disc of radius metres round its runestone, evenly spread (a loose cluster, not a ring), keeping clear metres off the stone itself; still inside their own area.

on.description: false: they attack at once, as before.

inviteWakes.description: a 💌 landing on one of a wild area's creatures wakes the area at once: its watch is over (or never starts), and its own young and adults, napping or not, wake with no getting up and go for her at once, by the hunt's rules (rules/inviteWakes.ts); its babies, legend and circle baby as before.

wildWatch.description: The wild watch: on a witch's first coming down on the ground in a wild area (not partified, not friendly, not home), its wild young and adults (not legends, the enraged or besiegers; babies keep their notice) hold off for time seconds, standing and turning to stare at her, any within hangBack metres backing off a little; then they fight as ever.

on.description: false: the old rule (only those near her attack).

hunt.description: The hunt: once a wild area's watch is over with her on the ground in it, every one of its own awake young and adults hunts her while she's in the area, wherever in it they are, never giving up or napping; over the treetops there they hold and come on again when she lands.

circle.description: a legend circle's baby naps at each pause with its own chance, for its own length (seconds), and is woken only by a witch on the ground within reach metres of its circle's edge (so she can still invite it), not anywhere in its area.

naps.description: Wild idlers nap: a wild creature roaming its own still-wild area (not besieging, fleeing, dazed, marching, fighting, happy or a legend), at each pause, lies down instead with chance, for length seconds (a range: min, max), then gets up.

guard.description: Parked party animals (at a sigil on the ground) guard it: they take on any wild creature of another kind within radius metres of the sigil, and come back to it.

babies.description: babies in every area, start's included, at most babyCap.

minHostile.description: at least this many young or adults in every wild area, any shortfall made up with young.

classes.description: strong (cap 6), medium (cap 12: swarm.reference, and every species not listed) and light (cap 16; Ed: "a swarm of 20 is too many; cap it at 16"), each class's strength 12 / its cap on its creatures' health and damage (strong ×2, light ×0.75; rules/combat/data.ts), so moving a species is one line here.

population.description: Wild creatures: every area starts with the same population, population.start, and, from the start, more by its place on the waves' route (Balance 2's shape; rules/growth.ts routePopulation): byRoute.threat, [route index, F] points (1 the first wave's stone; straight lines between, flat past the ends), is the extra fighting value its young and adults add (F by Lanchester, young 11.6, adult 40, babies 0; about what an area woken at that wave grew to before); its kind spends it by its profile (byRoute.profiles[species], else default: the shares of its extra creatures as babies, young and adults), so many more of a swarm's young than of a heavy kind's adults, at the same danger: count = threat ÷ the profile's mean F a creature × the area's count scale, rounded, split by the shares (largest remainder, ties by the seed).

creatureSpeeds.description: Ed: the witch is much faster than almost all creatures (she flies at groundSpeed, 19.25 m/s, on the ground and treetopSpeed, 48, over the treetops; at first 14 and 32).

legendCircle.description: A legend's circle: slow: while she stands on the ground in the circle of a legend asleep or restless, the world (the clock, the waves' countdown, the music, every creature, siege and timer) runs at scale of its speed, easing there and back over ease seconds as she crosses its edge; she and everything of hers (moving, blinking, rising and landing, her sigils, her 💌s and their cooldowns, her hat) keep full speed.

nightmare.description: a restless legend's one face, slightly sad to angry: faces[k] from restlessness at[k] on.

sleepy.description: while it sleeps giving its quest (its dream open, no nightmare), its face beside the sigil: mostly face (😴), and now and then, for one turn of every seconds, one of faces instead; each turn its own throw per legend (seeded by its id, so legends never change together), face with chance weight.

cycle.description: the pixel thought bubble shows one symbol for hold seconds, the face, then the sigil it dreams of, then the face again; a flask share of the sigil's turns (seeded per legend and turn) show the flask's relic sigil instead; each fades in and out over fade seconds.

dreams.description: A sleeping legend's dream (or nightmare) bubble, and its pointer to the nearest runestone of the area type it dreams of: shown only while she's on the ground within range metres of the legend (about its area's clearing and a little more); never from the treetops.

earlyQuest.description: one of the first three areas the waves wake (seeded), one with a legend, dreams of the baby of another of those three's kind (rules/quest.ts earlyQuest); if none of them has a legend, one of them (seeded, one whose kind another of the three lacks) is given one as the map is made, moved from the legend area the route reaches last (or, where that would clump legend areas together, from the one beside it), so share holds (rules/map.ts); false: every dream as before.

areas.description: on, each of the night's legends gets an area of its own grown out of the island beside one of its kind's areas (its pair), taking its kind and look, with no runestone, soundsystem or route stop, its circle at its heart; the island grows by them; the pair counts as one area for a legend's rage and for creatures attacking and defending (rules/map.ts areaOf); false: legends in their own kind's areas as before.

questRoll.description: (the same: "the difficulty of the encounter is the slot machine, not the reward size"): a done quest's buff is this many times as strong as written, whatever its dream's distance (it was 1 to 1.5 by distance, questFar; a relic's stays as written).

questLater.description: a legend dreams only of a kind living in an area later on the route than its own, within questCap areas; failing that, the kind of the nearest later area; with no later area, any kind (the early easy quest keeps its own pick); false: any kind as before.

bombard.description: ("Legend bombards, but prioritises you"): an angry legend with no witch in its reach throws the first lob or beam of its volley at the nearest standing soundsystem within range metres, damage a hit (of combat.soundsystemHealth); a charging legend lobs at it rather than charge.

stomp.description: on, a legend turning angry while its own area's soundsystem stands destroys it at once (ruined, as any fallen one), and legends are restless angryAfter seconds before they anger (legends.json angryAfter otherwise).

dark.description: a legend whose floored look (seen.floor times its coat's luminance, its body colour as baked: render/legendLight.ts) is under seen.dark has its floor raised to seen.dark over that luminance, at most seen.liftMax; the bear, the boar and the others as dark are caught, lighter legends stay as they are.

wildLegends.description: What legends are for: a mostly optional layer of tasks; quick players get buffs from their quests (open as long as a legend sleeps), lucky ones find relics for powerful allies, and a losing player sees their babies hurt in sieges and them enraged, the loss spiral faster and more dramatic (his words in DESIGN.md, "Legends, redesigned", and config/legends.json).

beat.description: The music's clock (beats per minute): the lasers sweep to it and party animals dance to it.

pulseSpeed.description: the pulse's speed along the route's own curves, metres a second, times the party's tempo (a knockdown's BPM speeds it); a wave lands as it reaches the next stone, so a wave's gap is its link's length over the speed; 0 holds the pulse where it is (no waves).

reveal.description: from the end of home's boot the line grows out from the treehouse along the route at this many links a wave (this many times the pulse's speed), a soft glow at its tip, reaching this stone as the first wave lands and going on at that pace until the whole route is drawn (so no stone pops on at once; rules/leypulse.ts leyReachTimes gives when it reaches each, for the beacons); none at all while home boots up.

advance.description: "first" moves it on when the next area's quest is done or its wave arrives, whichever comes first; "wave" only when its wave arrives.

brightness.description: how bright, a share of their first look, the glow through the crowns too.

depart.description: the first line leaves the treehouse's front round the ring of speakers, avoid metres outside it, on the first objective's side (clockwise on the screen and off to the right, the spiral starting east of home; the other way round for one west of it), then off the ring and looping round the same way out to the first objective; no link of the route passes over the dancefloor.

leyLines.description: The pause page's Waves slider sets it live, 0 to 6, remembered on this browser (config/decisions/953-waves.json, app/settings.ts); ?pulse=<m/s> or ?pulse=off sets it from a link, over the saved one.

exclude.description: pieces never placed, loose or in clusters.

generated.description: the prop generator's seeded bunting, balloon bunches and paper lanterns (art/party.js gen-*) in place of the hand-made ones they replace (the game turns it on: app/viewParams.ts).

partyObjects.description: Party objects: each partified area gets clusters [min, max] of the art's clusters, loose [min, max] loose pieces (litter, small lights, balloons; neon and balloon colours random per placement), set dressing at setChance, and at caughtChance an escaped balloon caught in a tree; hanging [min, max] lanterns, jars, fairy lights or mirror balls hung from branches in nearby crowns.

gaze.description: stargazing: beds from to to metres out past the speakers' ring, places side by side one behind another gap metres apart (lying along x, length metres long), each stagger metres along from the last, threes that share of beds (the rest pairs), apart metres between beds; a player keeping still within meet metres of one has the beach's turns with her (a chat, holding hands, a hug, lying side by side), turn seconds each.

partyWitches.description: Party witches: one per playing soundsystem (not the dancefloor's), however many, flying in from its side (from flyFrom metres out, at flyHeight, over arriveTime seconds) to land within roam metres of the dancefloor's middle (each new spot at roam × u^centreBias from it: the mean roam / (1 + centreBias), so the floor stays busiest), clear of trees, the speakers and the treehouse, and off again if it stops.

speakerLasers.description: The dancefloor ring's lasers: a single beam from each playing speaker, at most tilt degrees off straight up and leaning outwards, swinging sweep degrees sideways, over sweepBeats beats, neighbours out of phase; length metres, at opacity (thinner-looking than the area soundsystems' fans).

lasers.description: Each playing soundsystem's laser show: bursts of blockBars bars, on about duty of the time (seeded per soundsystem), up to maxCount beams stepping on the bars, fanned over spread degrees (no beam tilting more than maxTilt from straight up), swinging sweep degrees once every sweepBeats beats (slow, like searchlights), opening and closing the fan every openBars bars, length metres tall, opacity 0-1, fading in over fadeIn and out over fadeOut seconds, and fading with distance from fadeNear to fadeFar metres.

twinkle.description: (0 a gentle breathing, 1 star-like: brief flashes and dips, now and then a spark out for a moment); each spark flickers between its own area's colour and the one across the edge (Ed, v183), swapRate times a second on its own phase, and swapBeat of them snap on the beat instead.

borders.description: A sparkling line round the partified region's outside edge, in each area's sigil colour: width (px), brightness, sparkle (0-1, how much it twinkles and runs), step (metres between its sparks).

levelScale.description: a creature's bubble, emoji and outline together, times this by its level (baby, young, adult, legend); the witch's stays at 1.

bubbles.description: The talk's speech bubbles (Ed): an outline only, no fill.

variants.description: each area's stone one of the art's 20 seeded forms, dealt like a shuffled deck so every form is used before any repeats (Ed, #716; rules/runestones.ts) (height, lean, worn top, chips, cracks, moss, the carving's place and wear, the stones and grass at its foot), mirrored at random, its sigil never mirror-written; off, every stone as before.

lightRange.description: stones within this many metres light the scene.

runeMarkers.description: Spawn markers (Ed, v147): a rune stone on every spot where a soundsystem will come, scale times the old rune stone's size.

voices.description: the most one-shot sounds at once (0: no limit); over it, those that matter least (far creatures, the beds' scattered details) aren't played and lesser ones playing are cut short for her own sounds and the stings.

witch.description: each 💌 a syllable in her voice (pitch Hz, range: how far her phrases rise and fall, pace: a syllable's seconds, timbre: her formants over an adult's, phraseGap: a pause this long starts a new phrase).

animals.description: an attack a burst of babble in the creature's own voice (pitch Hz for a normal-sized young, lower by level and size; maxVoices at once, the farthest giving way (only to one swapBy nearer, at most one every swapGap seconds: a crowd otherwise cut itself off many times a second), duck: how much the others quieten; syllables per burst; gap: a creature speaks at most every gap seconds; reply: a 💌 hit's answering syllable, its volume share).

hit.description: a 💌 landing (a spent one a faint tick).

fill.description: the affection tick, climbing octaves as the meter fills.

enraged.description: the growl when one turns (gap: at most one every gap seconds, a crowd turning at once one heavier growl).

snore.description: a sleeping legend within range metres moaning softly in its dreams (volume).

windup.description: a legend's attack winding up, its whale song swelling for length seconds before it fires.

lost.description: a soundsystem lost, the sting heard anywhere (volume).

ouch.description: the witch hurt, her cry and a thump (volume; knocked down, her "whoa-oh" at knockdown times that), the music dipped by duck for duckTime seconds (twice that knocked down).

impact.description: a lobbed shot landing, a thud (small times volume) or a legend's boom (volume), heard from the lob's landing spot (a legend's twice as far).

roar.description: a legend turning angry, its roar (heard twice as far).

power.description: a runestone crackling into life as a speaker or soundsystem, heard within range metres: its static (crackle), a capacitor's whine, the mains buzz, the cone's thump and the clean tone it settles into, each the home ring's next step up the scale, the last a chord; at most one every gap seconds (volume).

lament.description: a restless legend calling out sadly, its own call lowered (pitch) and slowed (slow) into the legends' space, heard within range metres from the way of its clearing and muffled with distance; a call about every every seconds, down to urgent as its restlessness runs out; at most max restless legends call, the nearest, at least gap seconds apart (volume).

shoes.description: dancers within range metres tapping their party shoes on the beat, at most max at once.

pond.description: by a pond within range metres, water lapping (lap), a frog every frogEvery seconds or so (frogs), a drip every dripEvery (drips).

picnic.description: by a picnic in a partified area within range metres, its party-goers' murmur and cups clinking every clinkEvery seconds or so.

aggro.description: the wild watch's warning, while a wild area's watchers stand looking at her before they attack: a low swell in the music's key (swell) opening up and throbbing faster as the watch runs, a gritty riser over it (riser) by the area's danger, a hit as they attack (hit); called off, it sags and falls away over fall seconds; times volume.

sparkler.description: by the ley line's pulse, its tip a burning sparkler (art builder 2's #491), its fizz within range metres (louder as she nears it): a flickering hiss (hiss) and a crackle of pops (pops), rate sparks a second, a share fork of them forking into a double tick, times volume.

fireworks.description: over a soundsystem when a wave reaches an area she'd already cleared (Hotel's waveCelebrate, art builder 2's shells): each shell's climb (whoosh, now and then whistling), its burst (boom, its echo into the night echo, its stars' crackle), heard within range metres and late by the distance over speed metres a second, and the party under it cheering as the finale bursts (cheer) within cheerRange; the shells are rules/fireworks.ts's, the ones drawn, times volume.

seaLife.description: what lives in the sea off the beach, heard within range metres of it, under the music and the waves: a dolphin leaping off the east coast (splash: its blow and its splash back in), the kraken off the west coast (groan: a deep distant moan.

room.description: the creator's room in the treehouse while it's open, its hum, a record's crackle, the timber creaking every creakEvery seconds or so, and after the spell, at her decks before the first home speaker, at decks times its level.

deck.description: her decks while she stands behind them (the DJ witch): a stroke of the record on each half-beat of her scratch bars (scratch, its hiss under the stylus hiss, a stroke stroke seconds long) and her "woo-hoo!" when she throws a hand up (hype), and in her routine the tonearm's tick and the needle's drop (needle), times volume.

land.description: a 💌 that met no one landing on the ground, a soft puff (at most one every gap seconds).

nope.description: a soft two-note "uh-uh" at volume, at most one each gap seconds.

alarm.description: her phone ringing in the dark, a run of six bright plucks at volume, rung again every gap seconds while it rings.

cleared.description: a small "cleared!" sting on the next half-beat, at volume, from the new soundsystem, fading over range metres to no less than floor of itself (she cleared it: she hears it).

tempoUp.description: the crowd cheering on the beat the party starts speeding up, at volume (a share of the fireworks' cheer; 0 off).

stir.description: the boot-up over, the first wave's countdown begun, things stirring (volume).

knock.description: the witch knocked back (#108), a thump and a whoosh by how far (volume, whoosh), and stunned, a soft dizzy twinkle every twinkleEvery seconds (twinkle).

charge.description: a legend's long charge, its windup's bellow, heavy hoofbeats by its speed, the ground's rumble along its lane, the skid of its braking arc, a lighter trot home, heard within range metres.

relic.description: a relic bottle found (a rare chime), spotted within spot metres on the ground or spotTreetop from the treetops, or reached within reach.

meadow.description: home's ambience (breeze, bees, birds, a bird's song about every birdEvery seconds; its picnic's far murmur, its cups clinking about every clinkEvery seconds (clinks), its balloons squeaking about every squeakEvery (balloons)), in home's circle (the map's homeRadius round the dancefloor) fading out over its last fade metres.

whale.description: the legends' voice: volume, speed (1: moans of 2 to 3 s; 2: twice as fast), depth (Hz of its lowest moan), reverb (how big its space), sleepEvery (seconds between a sleeper's moans, sooner when restless).

sail.description: sailing between islands in place (app/sail.ts), the sea's hush and waves (sea, a share) and a soft gusting wind (wind) at volume while the next island is made, fading in and out over about fade seconds, the old night's music fading out over fade seconds as it comes in.

ambience.description: each area's own soundscape in play, the afterparty night's layers without their pad and bells (bed 0), its noise and sounds at noise and sounds, times volume; near the party it keeps only quiet of itself, by how loud the music is there, and gives way to the night once the party's over.

sadTrumpet.description: knocked down, a muted trumpet's "wah-wah-wah-waaah" as her hat drops, the music dipped by duck under it; knocked down with no hat to drop, its shorter "wah-waaah" if bare is 1 (0: none); and as she's whisked to her decks a backwards record scratch (rewind, times volume) cuts its last note off, never before that note has had cutAfter seconds.

sfx.description: The sound effects, all synthesised in the music's key: volume over the music's, hear metres (a sound fades to nothing that far from her).

latency.description: the audio context's latencyHint: interactive the smallest output buffer, balanced more room for the audio thread, playback the most (under-runs least likely, sound effects latest); ?latency= tries one for a load (DECISION FOR ED).

buffer.description: the audio output's buffer to ask for, in seconds, 0 for the latency category below; a browser that under-runs 20 times in a load asks for twice as much next load, up to 0.24 s (platform/audio/buffer.ts); the music goes out early by the context's latency so it stays on the beat shown, only the sound effects come later.

dropLayers.description: when her needle-drop routine ends after the party spell, that many of the intro's layers come in on the next bar line, each home speaker then adding its own on top.

radius.description: the clearing's metres round a legend where the map draws none.

circle.description: in a sleeping legend's clearing on the ground, the music muffled to muffle Hz and quiet times its volume, eased in and out with a time constant of ease seconds, and the legend's own layer (the music style's circle) over it at level.

muffle.description: on the house its low-pass closes to this many Hz as its world slows (eased with the slowing), its volume as it is; lighter than a legend circle's circle.muffle.

src.description: an audio file to loop (empty: the built-in loop at beat.bpm until there's a real track).

music.description: Music by proximity: one shared track, full and clear within nearDist metres of a playing soundsystem (or the dancefloor's ring, as loud as its speakers are on), fading to floor of the volume and muffled to a muffle Hz low-pass by farDist metres (clear: the cutoff close by), never gone; a damaged soundsystem nearby wobbles, crackles and drops out, by its damage times distort.

linger.description: seconds it stays after the last blow.

fall.description: seconds a fallen one stays, flashing then fading.

most.description: how many show at once (the most recently hit).

alarms.description: The soundsystem alarm: a soundsystem (or the home ring's speakers) hit while off screen shows a 🔇 at the screen's edge toward it, its ring its health, shaking at each blow.

transform.description: the seconds each takes to turn, glowing and rising into the speaker.

boot.description: At the start the home speaker ring boots up: its pulse runs from the treehouse's front down to the ring and once round it at speed m/s, each stone turning into its speaker as it passes; only then does the first wave's pulse set off: time to find and invite your first creatures.

motes.description: sparse glowing motes over every partified area, perPatch per 20 x 20 m, rising from from to to metres (under the crowns to above them) at about speed m/s.

uplight.description: crowns in partified areas catch a faint glow from below in the area's colour (strength at its brightest, pulse on the beat, fading over edge metres toward the border).

picker.description: how the next area to wake is chosen: route wakes them in one order worked out per map so the ley line through them all crosses itself at most a few times, within Ed's rules: a spiral.

noisy.description: (the picker before it, and the route's own fallback past the crossing rules) chooses among the areas bordering the party as below.

transition.description: seconds an area takes to partify, 0 to skip the show.

style.description: prints (footprints at its stride, left and right; four-legged ones in pairs, insects a tiny track; flyers, birds and snakes drip drops instead), prints+drops (and drops when badly hurt) or drops (drops only).

colour.description: red (a dark red on the night palette) or neon (a deep shade of the creature's own neon).

rate.description: drops a second at none of its health left (by how hurt, squared).

cap.description: marks at once (the oldest gives way).

blood.description: Blood trails: a hurt creature within range metres of her leaves small dark-red pixel marks on the ground as it moves, fading over fade seconds; the more hurt, the more often and the redder.

soundsystemGen.description: The generated soundsystems: each area's its own genome, dealt as one set a map (none alike).

more.description: times as many runs an area, their spread apart shrunk by its square root to fit (1 as tuned).

stringLights.description: Colourful string lights in every partified area, as long garlands: runsPerArea runs (a range), each spansPerRun spans (a range) from tree to tree, every next tree inside a forward cone of coneAngle degrees either side, so a run sweeps across rather than zig-zagging; runs start at least spread metres apart.

size.description: a digit's height as a share of the screen's.

lift.description: metres above the stone (or the treetops).

spent.description: how bright the number stays once the party has reached the area (0 hides it).

waveNumbers.description: Off; set on to true to bring them back.

tiles.description: the witch lights the tiles under her (in witchColour, from the neon) when below witchLift, with a ripple each beat lasting rippleTime seconds (a landing's twice as long), footsteps fading over trailTime, events (a wave arriving, a sigil placed) over eventTime, and at level 1 only lowLevelShare of the lit tiles show; through the boot the floor shows the island's sigil, written on stroke by stroke as the boot's pulse goes round the ring, in place of the moon, the sap rising up it every sapBars bars once written, until the first wave switches the floor on (on: false, the moon as before); a glowing magic circle (two hues 0-1, pulse per second, runeSpeed in turns per minute) lighting the ground round it (lightReach metres, lightStrength), a plaza of flagstones round the floor (paving: in rings from the rim out to beyond metres past the speakers' feet, course metres deep, stones about stone metres long, the outer edge breaking up over ragged metres with missing of its stones gone to grass, moss the share of mossy stones; the speakers stand on a course of darker stone); and a magic disco ball floating discoHeight metres up (discoSize metres across, spin turns per minute) throwing specks of light: specks is the share of the sphere that throws one, speckBrightness how bright, speckReach how far.

dancefloor.description: The dancefloor: motes: magic particles drifting up off the circle (count, how high they rise in metres, speed in m/s, column: the share of the circle they rise from); its radius in metres; a ring of speakers.count stone speakers (Ed, v160), the first at speakers.start degrees round from the camera side and the rest evenly spaced, speakers.radiusFactor times the radius out, each speakers.footprint metres round; a clear space of clearing metres beyond the speakers' feet (the treehouse stands outside that); the floor's glass tiles light up (Ed, v160): levels: how many areas must have the party for each level of intensity above 1 (up to 4, a full rave).

ease.description: seconds it eases in over (g.partyOver.ease, 0 to 1: the lights going out, the music winding down, the ley line fading to leyFloor of its brightness).

walk.description: their pace home, times their roaming speed (they walk, not run: a stroll home after the party).

partyOver.description: The party's over: once the home ring's speakers are all down, the afterparty, any soundsystem still standing switched off: the waves stop, nothing fights, and every creature walks home and sleeps.

sail.description: Sailing from the map table's sea chart (docs/plans/sail-without-reload.md, app/sail.ts): inPlace, the next night started on the same page (the old night's music fading out as a quiet sea and wind come in, sfx.sail; Back then opens the pause menu; anything going wrong loads the page anew, quietly), and so the bed and the bot game's exit, and the cards' Sea chart opening the map table's chart over the game; else the page loaded anew on the island's link (or chart.html) as before.

loading.description: The loading screen: the World Tree and COVEN RUSH in gold stars, lighting as the game loads, edge first by edge (0 plain random), at most rate stars a second, each flashing for flash seconds; ghost how bright the stars not yet lit show (0: an empty sky, Ed's call); the heart's star last, its supernova to white over nova seconds and the white clearing over clear seconds into the bedroom.

wake.description: the wake-up in her bedroom (rules/wakeUp.ts): snooze, a snooze's seconds (Ed: 5, as often as she likes); stretch, her stretch's seconds before she stands; alarmMin, the seconds the alarm rings before E can snooze it.

opening.description: The opening: bedroom, a plain first load (its link naming no seed or island, no arrival, no bot, the room not skipped) going straight to home's night and waking her in her bedroom there, asleep in the dark while the night is made.

handoff.description: where the chart hands over, sea metres out to sea off the south coast below the dancefloor (negative: inland), its camera dist metres back and pitchDeg degrees down (the first flight's: -40, 600, 50); ?dive=near|far|skim for one load (app/chartView.ts DIVES).

tree.description: after framing the dancefloor, the camera comes round to the whole treehouse tree from the south, angle degrees up at its middle, far enough back that it fills fill of the frame's height (its height in metres from its art once drawn, height till then), time seconds after the frame, then settle seconds on into her bedroom.

arrive.description: Arriving on an island from the sea chart: the chart hands off over the open sea south of the island (its last frame and camera in sessionStorage, Charlie's chart side), the page shows that still pushing in (a CSS animation in index.html, from the first paint) while the night builds, then cross-fades it away over fade seconds into the game's camera at the same place, and flies on, looking north: over the sea and low over the forest at speed m/s (low: angle degrees down, distance metres back, aimed offshore metres past the south coast at first; each low leg at least minLeg seconds), then up over rise seconds to frame the dancefloor and the treehouse's spot together (frame: angle, distance, lift metres over the ground), then down over settle seconds into the opening shot at her decks.

zoomEase.description: how softly zoom and rising change the angle and distance.

beyond.description: how many metres past the bent ground's horizon the distant treetops are still drawn (fewer is cheaper).

curve.description: the world bends away toward the top of the screen, per metre ahead of the witch, eased in as she rises; ?curve=<treetop> tries values (0.0015: about 11% of the screen sky in ?bare=1, Ed v276 asked 10-12%; 0.0022 about 24%; under 0.001 none; 0 off).

speedZoom.description: the treetop camera's distance is times (treetopSpeed / base) to the power power, so at a faster treetopSpeed it zooms out and the screen holds about as many seconds of flight (power 0: off).

shake.description: each hit adds trauma (0-1), base on her first, perMissingHit more for each hit she was already missing, knockdown on the hit that knocks her down; it falls away at decay a second, and the screen shakes by trauma squared times maxOffsetPx (screen pixels, whole ones) and maxRotDeg, smooth noise wandering speed times a second.

circle.description: on the ground in a legend's circle the camera eases over ease seconds to angle degrees (from the ground view's 30 to 36), its distance times distance, aimed frame of the way from her to the legend and look metres higher, so the legend stands large over her; it eases back as she leaves.

house.description: landed on the treehouse's floor, the camera eases over ease seconds to angle degrees and its distance times distance.

aim.description: with no part, the camera aimed that share of her height (as she's drawn) up her.

parts.description: for the part of her the row in focus is about (config/wardrobe.json's frame: head, hat, top, legs, feet, broom; board, the Workshop's pegboard, the wall behind her, so aimed up over her to it), aimed aim of her height (as drawn: 0 her feet, 1 the top of her hat) up her and look metres higher (a thing by her: the board, the broom), and its distance times distance in place of the station's own, eased from part to part as the cursor moves.

station.description: at a dressing station and choosing (the pointer or the d-pad in its panel, or stood still a moment: ui/stationPanel.ts), its distance times distance and moved side times that distance east (west when negative), so she stands clear of the panel; eased over ease seconds, and back as soon as she moves.
